questions.stem: For each pressure injury description, select the stage.

cells.text: Intact skin with redness that doesn't blanch over the sacrum
Shallow open area with a pink-red wound bed and no slough
Full-thickness loss with visible fat but no bone or tendon
Wound bed covered by eschar so the depth can't be seen

rationale.correct: Stage pressure injuries by the deepest tissue visible; slough or eschar that hides the base makes the injury unstageable.

perOption.b1:a: Intact skin with non-blanchable redness is stage 1.
perOption.b1:b: This description fits stage 1, not stage 2.
perOption.b1:c: This description fits stage 1, not stage 3.
perOption.b1:d: This description fits stage 1, not stage 4.
perOption.b1:e: This description fits stage 1, not unstageable.
perOption.b2:a: This description fits stage 2, not stage 1.
perOption.b2:b: Partial-thickness skin loss with a pink-red bed is stage 2.
perOption.b2:c: This description fits stage 2, not stage 3.
perOption.b2:d: This description fits stage 2, not stage 4.
perOption.b2:e: This description fits stage 2, not unstageable.
perOption.b3:a: This description fits stage 3, not stage 1.
perOption.b3:b: This description fits stage 3, not stage 2.
perOption.b3:c: Full-thickness skin loss with visible fat is stage 3.
perOption.b3:d: This description fits stage 3, not stage 4.
perOption.b3:e: This description fits stage 3, not unstageable.
perOption.b4:a: This description fits stage 4, not stage 1.
perOption.b4:b: This description fits stage 4, not stage 2.
perOption.b4:c: This description fits stage 4, not stage 3.
perOption.b4:d: Exposed bone, tendon or muscle is stage 4.
perOption.b4:e: This description fits stage 4, not unstageable.
perOption.b5:a: This description fits unstageable, not stage 1.
perOption.b5:b: This description fits unstageable, not stage 2.
perOption.b5:c: This description fits unstageable, not stage 3.
perOption.b5:d: This description fits unstageable, not stage 4.
perOption.b5:e: Slough or eschar that hides the base makes it unstageable.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which Braden scale score shows the highest risk for pressure injury?

rationale.correct: Braden scale: 6 to 23 points; a lower score means a higher risk.

perOption.a: Lower Braden scores mean higher risk; 9 or below is very high risk.
perOption.d: This is the highest possible score, meaning lowest risk.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which interventions help prevent pressure injuries in a client on bed rest? Select all that apply.

options.text: Reposition the client at least every 2 hours
Keep the head of the bed at 30 degrees or lower unless contraindicated
Float the heels off the bed

rationale.correct: Prevention: reposition, reduce shear, support surfaces, manage moisture, good nutrition, no massage or donuts.

perOption.a: This relieves pressure.
perOption.b: This reduces shear on the sacrum.
perOption.d: Massage can damage the tissue further.
perOption.e: Donuts reduce blood flow to the surrounding tissue.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client coughs, and loops of bowel come out through the abdominal incision. What should the nurse do first?

options.text: Cover the wound with sterile gauze moistened with sterile saline
Push the bowel back into the abdomen
Help the client walk to reduce pressure

rationale.correct: Evisceration: cover with saline-moistened sterile dressings, low Fowler's position with knees bent, stay with the client and notify the surgeon.

perOption.a: This protects the organs and keeps them moist.
perOption.c: Dry gauze sticks to and damages tissue.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: Wound drainage is thin, watery and pale pink. How should the nurse document it?

rationale.correct: Serous = clear; sanguineous = bloody; serosanguineous = pink; purulent = pus.

perOption.a: Serosanguineous drainage is a mix of serum and blood.
perOption.b: Purulent drainage is thick and yellow, green or tan.
perOption.c: Sanguineous drainage is bright red blood.
perOption.d: Serous drainage is clear and straw-colored.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which nutrients are most important to promote wound healing?

rationale.correct: Wound healing needs protein, calories, vitamin C, zinc and fluids.

perOption.a: These support collagen synthesis and tissue repair.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: How should the nurse obtain a wound culture?

options.text: Clean the wound with sterile saline first, then swab viable tissue
Swab the old drainage on the dressing
Apply an antiseptic and swab right away

rationale.correct: Wound culture: clean with saline, then swab clean viable tissue (Levine technique).

perOption.a: Cleaning removes surface contaminants so the culture reflects the infection.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: Using the rule of nines, calculate the total body surface area burned for an adult with burns to the entire front of the trunk, the entire left arm and the front of the right leg.

rationale.correct: Front of trunk = 18%. Entire left arm = 9%. Front of right leg = 9%. Total = 18 + 9 + 9 = 36%.
references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Estimate burn size with the rule of nines.

questions.stem: A client was rescued from a house fire. Which finding is the priority?

options.text: Singed nasal hair, soot around the mouth and a hoarse voice

rationale.correct: Inhalation injury threatens the airway; prepare for early intubation.

perOption.a: These suggest inhalation injury, and airway swelling can progress quickly.
perOption.b: This is important but not an airway threat.
perOption.c: Pain needs treatment after the airway is assessed.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: An 80 kg client has burns over 36% of the body. Using the Parkland formula (4 mL × kg × %TBSA), how many mL of lactated Ringer's should the client receive in the first 8 hours after the burn?

rationale.correct: Total 24-hour volume = 4 × 80 × 36 = 11,520 mL. Half is given in the first 8 hours = 5,760 mL.
references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Calculate burn fluid resuscitation with the Parkland formula.

questions.stem: Which finding best shows that fluid resuscitation is adequate in an adult with major burns?

options.text: Urine output of 0.5 mL/kg/hr (about 30 to 50 mL/hr)

rationale.correct: Titrate burn fluids to urine output (0.5 mL/kg/hr for adults; higher for electrical injury).

perOption.a: Urine output is the main guide for titrating burn fluids.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: During the first 24 hours after a major burn, which laboratory finding should the nurse expect?

rationale.correct: Emergent phase: hyperkalemia, hemoconcentration and metabolic acidosis.

perOption.a: Cell damage releases potassium, and plasma loss concentrates the blood.
perOption.b: These are more typical later, during fluid mobilization.
perOption.c: Albumin falls as it leaks out.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Predict lab changes in the emergent burn phase.

questions.stem: A client has full-thickness burns all the way around the lower leg. Which finding requires immediate action?

options.text: Weakening pedal pulse and increasing numbness in the foot
Dry, leathery appearance of the burn
Little pain in the burned area

rationale.correct: Burns that circle a limb need frequent neurovascular checks.

perOption.a: Tight eschar can cut off circulation; an escharotomy may be needed.
perOption.b: This is expected with full-thickness burns.
perOption.c: Nerve endings are destroyed in full-thickness burns.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: How should pain medication be given to a client in the emergent phase of a major burn?

rationale.correct: Give burn pain medication IV in the acute phase.

perOption.a: Poor perfusion makes IM and subcutaneous absorption unreliable.
perOption.c: The GI tract may be slowed.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Choose the route for burn analgesia.

questions.stem: A client with burns is treated with silver sulfadiazine cream. Which laboratory value should the nurse monitor?

rationale.correct: Silver sulfadiazine: watch for leukopenia and sulfa allergy.

perOption.a: Silver sulfadiazine can cause transient leukopenia.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which diet supports healing for a client with major burns?

rationale.correct: Burns cause hypermetabolism; meet needs with high calories and protein, often by early enteral feeding.

perOption.a: Burns greatly increase metabolic needs.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which intervention helps prevent contractures in a client with burns over the joints?

options.text: Positioning the joints in extension and using splints as prescribed

rationale.correct: Burn rehabilitation: extension positioning, splints and ROM exercises.

perOption.a: This keeps tissue from shortening during healing.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client has an electrical burn with small entry and exit wounds. What is the priority?

rationale.correct: Electrical burns: cardiac monitoring and watching for myoglobinuria (higher urine output goals).

perOption.a: Electrical current can cause dysrhythmias.
perOption.b: The visible wounds underestimate the internal damage.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Prioritize care for an electrical burn.

questions.stem: A worker splashes a strong chemical on the arm. What should the nurse do first?

options.text: Flush with large amounts of water for at least 20 minutes

rationale.correct: Chemical burns: remove contaminated clothing (brush off dry powders first) and irrigate thoroughly.

perOption.a: Flushing removes the chemical and stops the burn.
perOption.b: Neutralizing can cause a heat reaction.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client has cellulitis of the lower leg. Which action helps the team track its progression?

options.text: Mark the border of the redness with a skin marker and note the time

rationale.correct: Cellulitis: mark borders, elevate, give antibiotics and watch for systemic signs.

perOption.a: This shows whether the redness is spreading or shrinking.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which mole should the client have checked by a provider?

options.text: A mole with uneven borders and several colors that has grown recently
A small, round, evenly brown mole that hasn't changed
A freckle that fades in winter
A skin tag on the neck

rationale.correct: ABCDE: Asymmetry, Border, Color, Diameter over 6 mm, Evolving.

perOption.a: Asymmetry, irregular borders, color variation and change suggest melanoma (ABCDE).
perOption.b: This is a typical benign mole.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which instruction helps prevent skin cancer?

options.text: Use a broad-spectrum sunscreen of SPF 30 or higher and limit sun exposure between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m.
Use tanning beds to build a base tan
Use sunscreen only on cloudy days
Apply sunscreen once a day only

rationale.correct: Sun safety: sunscreen, protective clothing, shade and no tanning beds.

perOption.a: This reduces UV damage.
perOption.c: UV exposure occurs on all days.
perOption.d: Reapply every 2 hours and after swimming.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old is starting isotretinoin for severe acne. Which teaching is most important?

options.text: Use two forms of contraception, because the drug causes severe birth defects
Expect the acne to clear in 2 days

rationale.correct: Isotretinoin: teratogenic, mood changes, dry skin and lips, no vitamin A and no blood donation.

perOption.a: Isotretinoin is highly teratogenic; programs require pregnancy prevention and testing.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which action helps prevent skin tears in an older adult?

options.text: Use a lift sheet to move the client and avoid strong adhesive tape
Drag the client up in bed
Use strong adhesive tape on the skin
Bathe with hot water twice a day

rationale.correct: Skin tear prevention: lift sheets, padding, gentle handling, moisturizers and silicone tape.

perOption.a: Fragile skin tears with friction and adhesive removal.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Prevent skin tears in older adults.

questions.stem: The nurse reviews a surgical wound assessment. Highlight the findings that suggest infection.

cells: Thick, yellow-green, with a foul odor
Redness extending 3 cm beyond the incision

rationale.correct: Signs of wound infection: purulent drainage, spreading erythema, warmth, increasing pain and fever.

perOption.r3: Fever several days after surgery suggests wound infection.
perOption.r4: Granulation tissue is a sign of healing.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
